turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I... I feel that both of you are speaking from your hearts, but isn't there a way for us to find common ground?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your intentions may be clear to you, Sandip, but they are causing unrest among my people. I am not afraid to act against threats, and I will not hesitate to take action to protect my tenants from your influence.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I understand your concerns, Nikhil, and I see Sandip's passion as well. Can we perhaps discuss this without hostility?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Bimala, always the voice of peace and harmony. But Nikhil, your threats and accusations sting like the first rain of autumn. If you believe my actions are oppressive, then surely the hearts of the people will show their true colors. Let us see whose influence truly resonates with the masses.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your actions speak louder than your words, Sandip. The people may be swayed by empty rhetoric, but I will not allow them to suffer under your rule. I demand you cease your harmful activities immediately.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Nikhil, your demands are like the rustling of leaves before the storm. But fear not, for the people's hearts are not leaves to be blown by any wind. They seek a leader who will guide them to a brighter future, and I am that beacon.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your rhetoric may inspire some, Sandip, but it does not change the fact that your actions harm my people. I will not stand idly by and watch them suffer.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your heart is pure but your vision is narrow. I see the fire in your eyes, the passion that you hold, but you must understand that change often comes with conflict. It is the nature of our time.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I... I see the passion in both of your hearts, but I am worried about the division it might cause. Can we not find a way to unite instead of dividing?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Unity is indeed desirable, Bimala, but it cannot be achieved through oppression and deceit. Sandip, your methods may claim to serve the greater good, but they harm the very people they aim to help.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I understand your concerns, Nikhil. But Sandip speaks with a fervor that ignites hope in many hearts. Perhaps there is a way for us to channel that energy towards positive change without causing harm.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your words are like a cool breeze in a hot summer, but they miss the fire that burns within the hearts of the people. Bimala, you are the voice of reason, but even reason needs a spark to ignite change. Let us not forget that the path to a better future is often paved with the embers of conflict.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip, your rhetoric is stirring but it is a dangerous game you play. The embers you speak of could ignite a wildfire that consumes everything in its path. Cease your oppressive actions or face the consequences.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Nikhil, your caution is as predictable as it is noble. But let me remind you, it is the bold who make history, not the timid. I will not let the fear of a wildfire extinguish the fire of progress.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, Nikhil, I see the value in both your perspectives. Perhaps there is a middle ground where we can walk together, where neither the cool breeze nor the wildfire prevails.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Bimala, my dearest, your wisdom is as ever a beacon of light. Yet, in the arena of politics, one must wield a sword as well as a pen. Nikhil, you speak of consequences, but remember, it is the lion's roar that reverberates through the jungle, not the whispers of the deer.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, Nikhil, I find myself torn between the lion's roar and the cool breeze. Can we not seek a path where compassion and courage coexist?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Bimala, I respect your desire for balance, but do not let Sandip's fiery rhetoric cloud your judgment. His actions are a threat not just to my lands, but to the stability of our community.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your caution is as noble as it is narrow-minded. The path of progress is not paved with caution but with the bold steps of visionaries. And Bimala, my dear, you are the embodiment of the balance you seek.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, Nikhil, I feel caught in a storm, unable to find shelter. Can we not find a way to calm the tempest without extinguishing the fire of progress?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ... No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
